source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: According to Ruth B. Freeman, what is the focus of community health nursing services?
questions.rationale: Freeman described CHN as a service rendered by a professional nurse with communities, groups, families, and individuals in homes, health centers, clinics, schools, and workplaces for health promotion, illness prevention, and care of the sick at home and rehabilitation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 79)
questions.quote: Care of the sick at home and rehabilitation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Dr. C.E. Winslow defined public health as the science and art of which three aims?
questions.rationale: Winslow defined public health as the science and art of preventing disease, prolonging life, and promoting health and efficiency through organized community effort.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 79)
questions.quote: According to Dr. C.E Winslow, public health is the science and art of

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is the public health nurse of a rural health unit in Iloilo.
questions.stem: Nurse Carla motivates barangay residents and starts community development activities. Which PHN role is she performing?
questions.rationale: As community organizer, the PHN motivates and enhances community participation and initiates and participates in community development activities.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 79)
questions.quote: Motivates and enhances community participation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is the public health nurse of a rural health unit in Iloilo.
questions.stem: Nurse Carla trains the rural health midwives in her catchment area. Which role is this?
questions.rationale: The health educator/counselor/trainer role includes health teaching, counseling, and training and educating rural health midwives.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 80)
questions.quote: Trains and educates rural health midwives

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nurse Carla is the public health nurse of a rural health unit in Iloilo.
questions.stem: Nurse Carla updates the RHU database and analyzes the data for interpretation. Which role is she performing?
questions.rationale: The reporter/recorder/statistician records nursing interventions, updates the database, and makes statistical analysis of data for interpretation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing (PDF p. 80)
questions.quote: Makes statistical analysis of data for interpretation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the Local Government Code (RA 7160), what happened to health services from the provincial level down to the barangay?
options: They were devolved to the LGUs
questions.rationale: RA 7160 devolved all structures, personnel, and budgetary allocations from the provincial health level down to the barangays to the local government units.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Local Health System (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: All structures, personnel, and budgetary allocations from the provincial health level down to the barangays were DEVOLVED

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: What is the ideal population size of an inter-local health zone (health district)?
questions.rationale: An ideal health district has a population of 100,000 to 500,000 for optimum efficiency and effectiveness.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Local Health System (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: Ideal health district would have a population size between 100,000 to 500,000

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Primary health care was adopted in the Philippines through which issuance?
questions.rationale: PHC was adopted through Letter of Instruction 949, signed by President Marcos on October 19, 1979.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: Signed by President Marcos on October 19, 1979

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which is one of the four cornerstones (pillars) of primary health care?
questions.rationale: The four cornerstones are active community participation, intra- and inter-sectoral linkages, use of appropriate technology, and support mechanisms made available.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: Active community participation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which is an element of primary health care in the ELEMENTS mnemonic?
questions.rationale: ELEMENTS: Education for health, Locally endemic disease control, EPI, Maternal and child health and family planning, Essential drugs, Nutrition, Treatment, and Sanitation of the environment.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: E Ssential Drugs

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A trained barangay health worker is which level of primary health care worker?
questions.rationale: Village/barangay health workers include trained community health workers, health auxiliary volunteers, and traditional birth attendants or healers. PHNs, midwives, and rural health physicians are intermediate level.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Primary Health Care (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: Refers to trained community health workers or health auxiliary volunteer or a traditional birth attendant or healer

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A rural health unit and a barangay health station belong to which level of care?
questions.rationale: Primary care facilities include barangay health stations, rural health units, community hospitals, health centers, and puericulture centers.
explanations: Not in the PH referral levels.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Health Care (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: Barangay Health Stations

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A district hospital that does minor surgery and simple laboratory tests and receives RHU referrals is at which level?
questions.rationale: Secondary care serves as the referral center for primary facilities, can do minor surgery and simple laboratory exams, and includes district and provincial hospitals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Health Care (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: Capable of performing minor surgeries and perform some simple laboratory examinations

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Sputum AFB testing of a coughing client is which level of prevention?
questions.rationale: Secondary prevention is early detection and prompt treatment, such as diagnostic tests (AFB) and breast self-examination.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Prevention (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Focuses on early detection of disease and prompt treatment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Teaching crutch walking to a client after a leg amputation is which level of prevention?
questions.rationale: Tertiary prevention is rehabilitation to prevent further disability and restore optimum function, such as crutch walking and physical therapy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Prevention (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Rehabilitation (prevent further disability)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Families (Normal & At Risk)
questions.stem: A family's breadwinner is about to retire with no other income source. In family assessment, this is a:
questions.rationale: A foreseeable crisis is an anticipated period of unusual demand on the family in terms of resources and adjustment.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Anticipated periods of unusual demand on the individual/family in terms of resources and adjustment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Families (Normal & At Risk)
questions.stem: A family keeps an open drum of stagnant water where mosquitoes breed. This is a:
questions.rationale: A health threat is a condition that promotes disease or injury and keeps people from reaching their health potential.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Condition that promote disease or injury and prevent people from realizing their health potential

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Families (Normal & At Risk)
questions.stem: A child in the family has a developmental lag. This is a:
questions.rationale: A health deficit is a gap between actual and achievable health, such as an existing disease, disability, or developmental lag.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Already developed the disease or disability, developmental lag.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In the community health nursing process, when are the evaluation parameters developed?
questions.rationale: Developing evaluation parameters is done in the planning stage, as part of the operational plan.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Community Health Nursing Process (PDF p. 83)
questions.quote: Development of evaluation parameters is done in the planning stage

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which management function establishes standards, measures performance, and corrects deviations?
questions.rationale: Controlling measures and corrects activities and sets standards so objectives are met: establish standards, measure performance, and correct deviations.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Management Functions of the CHN (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Process that measures and corrects the activities of the people and establishes standards so that objectives are met

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: During an RHU clinic day, which case does the nurse refer to the physician during triage?
options: A child with simple diarrhea under IMCI
A TB client on DOTS refill
questions.rationale: In triaging, program-based cases are managed according to protocols, and all non-program-based cases are referred to the physician.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Clinic Visit (PDF p. 84)
questions.quote: Refer all non-program based cases to the physician

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.stem: Before measuring BP at the health center, how long should the client have avoided smoking and caffeine?
questions.rationale: The client should rest for 5 minutes and should not have smoked or taken caffeine within 30 minutes before BP measurement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Pressure Measurement (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: Client should not have smoked or ingested caffeine within 30 minutes before BP measurement

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.stem: On a client's first BP visit, the readings differ between arms. Which arm is used for later readings?
options: The arm with the higher reading
The arm with the lower reading
questions.rationale: On the first visit, BP is taken in both arms; subsequent readings use the arm with the higher reading.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Pressure Measurement (PDF p. 85)
questions.quote: Subsequent BP readings should be performed on the arm, with a higher BP reading

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Families (Normal & At Risk)
questions.stem: Which factor is MOST important in deciding how often to make home visits?
questions.rationale: The needs of the family are the most important factor in home visit frequency, followed by the family's acceptance.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Home Visit (PDF p. 86)
questions.quote: Needs of the (most important)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Families (Normal & At Risk)
questions.stem: During a home visit, what does the nurse do right after stating the purpose of the visit?
questions.rationale: Steps: greet and introduce self, state the purpose, observe the client and determine needs, place the bag and do bag technique, give care and teaching, record, and set a return visit.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Home Visit (PDF p. 86)
questions.quote: Observe the patient and determine health needs

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Families (Normal & At Risk)
questions.stem: What is the MAIN principle of bag technique?
questions.rationale: Bag technique should minimize, if not prevent, the spread of infection. It may vary with agency policy or the home situation as long as this principle is observed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bag Technique (PDF p. 86)
questions.quote: Minimize if not prevent the spread of any infection

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which type of epidemiology tests hypotheses to find the causes of a disease?
questions.rationale: Analytical epidemiology analyzes causes or determinants of disease through hypothesis testing. Descriptive covers distribution and frequency.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Epidemiology (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Attempts to analyze causes or determinants of disease through hypothesis testing

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which rate is considered a good index of the general health condition of a community?
questions.rationale: The infant mortality rate is a good index of the general health condition of a community.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Good index of the general health condition of a community

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which measure is the index of the killing power of a disease?
questions.rationale: The case fatality ratio indexes the killing power of a disease. It is affected by incomplete reporting and poor morbidity data.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Index of a killing power of a disease

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A barangay counts ALL existing dengue cases, new and old, on one day. Which measure is this?
questions.rationale: Prevalence measures the proportion of the population with a disease at a particular time, counting new and old cases. Incidence counts new cases only.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Measures the proportion of population which exhibits a particular disease at a particular time

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which rate measures pregnancy wastage?
questions.rationale: The fetal death rate measures pregnancy wastage: death of the product of conception before complete expulsion, regardless of pregnancy duration.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vital Statistics (PDF p. 87)
questions.quote: Measures pregnancy wastage
